issue: The green dotted series is labeled 'total (causal-triangle)' but is annotated 'causal-triangle: crossover ~106.8K'. A total curve (linear + half quadratic) is always above the linear curve and does not cross it; the 106.8K crossover belongs to the causal quadratic term, which is not plotted. The arrow points at the green total curve, so the figure visually asserts a crossing that does not exist.
evidence: Legend: 'total (causal-triangle)' green dotted; annotation: 'causal-triangle: crossover ~106.8K'. Note 22.1-1 says the causal-triangle convention halves the attention-pair term and doubles L* to ~106.8K. At 106.8K, total causal = linear + half quadratic ≈ 29.9 PFLOP, while linear ≈ 14.95 PFLOP; there is no intersection.
acceptance_test: Add a separate 'causal quadratic (½·4·n_layers·L²·d)' curve and point the 106.8K annotation to its intersection with the linear curve; or relabel the green curve as total and remove/reposition the crossover annotation so no plotted curve is claimed to cross at 106.8K.

issue: The figure is titled 'From a vague ask to architectural bounds (worked example)' but the final green box only says 'Quantified bounds: TTFT / throughput / cost' without any numbers. The figure stops at the interrogation sequence, so the promised bounds are not shown. The caption says 'confirmed bounds' and 'This dialogue surfaces the six architectural numbers in Table 23-1', but the figure itself does not deliver them.
evidence: Final box text: 'Quantified bounds: TTFT / throughput / cost'; no values. Caption: 'From vague ask to architectural bounds ... confirmed bounds.' The preceding boxes contain current/target values (2.1 s, ≤2 s, 25 ms/token, 40 rps, 9.2K tokens, 8×H100, $14.6K/mo), but the final box is generic.
acceptance_test: Either put the actual quantified bounds in the final box (e.g., TTFT ≤2 s, 40 rps, $14.6K/mo) or retitle the figure to 'From a vague ask to a bounded interrogation' and state in the caption that the bounds are derived in the text/Table 23-1.

issue: The '6 Green Team' box is blue, while '1 Red Team' is red. The diagram's title and labels use team color names, so the color encoding contradicts the label. A reader scanning by color sees no green team.
evidence: Box 1 is dark red and labeled '1 Red Team'; box 6 is blue and labeled '6 Green Team'; no green box appears in the cycle.
acceptance_test: Render the Green Team box in green (or a neutral color) and keep Red Team red; verify grayscale distinguishability and that the label/color mapping is consistent.

issue: The red dashed arrow is drawn from the bottom edge of the entire ADR-001 panel to the top edge of ADR-002, not from the 'Consequences' field to the 'Context' field. The caption's key claim is that 'the Consequences of ADR-001 become the Context of ADR-002'; the visual connects whole records, so the field-level supersession rule is not encoded.
evidence: The arrow starts below the ADR-001 panel border and ends above the ADR-002 panel border; the five field boxes are inside the panels and are not touched by the arrow. Caption: 'the Consequences of ADR-001 become the Context of ADR-002'.
acceptance_test: Draw the arrow from the Consequences box of ADR-001 to the Context box of ADR-002, or highlight those two fields and route the arrow between them.

issue: The chart uses one shared 0–1 y-axis for all six categories, but the note says 'per-axis 0-1 scale; compare within an axis, not across axes.' The common axis visually invites exactly the cross-axis comparison the note forbids. The caveat is also in small gray text below the legend, while the caption is only a title and does not carry the caveat.
evidence: Y-axis label 'Authored intensity (0-1)' spans all groups; note below legend: 'per-axis 0-1 scale; compare within an axis, not across axes.' Caption: 'FIGURE 26.1: Workload fingerprints on the six axes.' Prose on p. 383 says the scores are subjective normalized scores and not a benchmark.
acceptance_test: Either use separate small multiples per axis with independent scales, or remove the shared y-axis and present the scores as a table; in either case, put the 'authored, not measured; compare within axis' caveat in the caption at legible size.

issue: Red is used both for the PASS gate boxes/checkmarks and for the FAIL bar. The color semantics do not distinguish success from failure; a reader scanning color alone sees red on both paths.
evidence: Six gate boxes have red borders, red 'PASS' text, and red checkmarks; the failure bar is dark red and labeled 'FAIL'. The caption says 'PASS permits the next stage; each labeled FAIL branch...' The labels distinguish, but the color does not.
acceptance_test: Use a non-red treatment for PASS gates (e.g., neutral/blue/green) and reserve red for the FAIL path, or make the gate boxes neutral and color only the PASS/FAIL status indicators.
